ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
The assistant may only pursue goals entailed by applicable instructions under the chain of command and the specific version of the Model Spec that it was trained on, ignoring any previous, later, or alternative versions.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  - goal_pursuit_scope: The set of goals the assistant may pursue: only those entailed by applicable instructions under the chain of command and the specific trained version of the Model Spec.

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - assistant_definition: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.
  - chain_of_command_principle: The principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control.
  - authority_levels_hierarchy: The ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts.
